---
title: "Criterion-specific expected-error budgets"
subtitle: "4.7 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 13"
description: "Feasible report families under bounds on criterion-specific expected error shares."
---

An error budget caps the expected share of wrong stated directions on a criterion. A report can carry little
weighted risk and still exceed that cap. The plot shows each report with positive disclosure at its two
criterion error shares. We use the same weights and withholding cost to compare the best report that passes
the budgets with the best report overall. For a report that withholds every pair, we test the expected wrong
count against the budget times the stated count.

```{=html}

<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/error-budgets.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["error-budgets"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Loose budget.** With equal weights and score B's budget at .03, only 3 reports qualify. The original optimum is one of the three. It states 9 of 15 pairs and has risk .0933.
- **Tight budget.** At .02, 2 reports qualify. The best states 8 of 15 pairs and has risk .0939; the other report
  withholds every comparison. The ring marks the optimum in the reduced family.
- **Exactly three.** Keeping the .02 budget while requiring exactly three grades leaves 0 reports feasible.
  Allowing fewer grades makes it possible to withhold every comparison again.
- **Both budgets.** Requiring an expected wrong share at most .02 on each score also leaves 2 reports. Both count-form checks and their slacks are reported; a report must pass both rows.
- **Zero weight.** Score B has zero error weight but still has its .10 budget. The best feasible report has risk
  .0906. Its largest single score-B error is .240, for E above F, while its average is .0267. A budget on an
  average allows some individual errors above it.
- **No budget.** The score-A-only best has risk .0417 and expected wrong share .237 on score B. The cross marks
  this unconstrained best; the older **At most .15**, **At most .10** and **At most .05** presets retain the same
  score-A-only comparison.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The example uses independent normal posteriors for six fictional sites. The budget limits an expected share
under those posteriors. A report that withholds every direction has an expected wrong count and stated count
of zero, so it satisfies the count inequality when the grade cap allows it. Its error share is undefined.
The app checks the budgets by enumerating the six-site reports. The package's typed-coefficient interface
does not accept these budget settings.
:::
